guard: a provider-induced Harness API close during a delivered mesh turn leaves the seat alive after a transient replacement failure only when that failed tree is proven stopped; unproven teardown is terminal before another launch, and a second disconnect remains terminal
_note: The first failure is deliberately after a real mesh delivery and real Unix-socket close. The replacement then loses one synthetic attach race before the same bounded recovery window succeeds. The final close proves the design did not become an unbounded relaunch loop.

mutations.name: M1 restore the shipped defect: close exits the seat without recovery
mutations.cell: the recovery attempt deterministically loses its first attach race (#971)

mutations.name: M2 replace a disconnected client but forget the owned session
mutations.cell: the recovery attempt deterministically loses its first attach race (#971)

mutations.name: M3 attach the replacement but leave the broken client active
mutations.replace: /* mutant: replacement is never made active */
mutations.cell: recovered seat redrives the unacknowledged stalled turn (#781)

mutations.name: M4 restore the shipped losing-race exit: one transient replacement failure kills the seat
mutations.expectRed: provider disconnect survives a transient replacement loss inside the bounded recovery window (#971)
mutations.cell: provider disconnect survives a transient replacement loss inside the bounded recovery window (#971)

mutations.name: M5 retry without proving the failed replacement tree stopped
mutations.expectRed: the failed transient replacement is stopped before the successful retry
mutations.cell: the failed transient replacement is stopped before the successful retry

mutations.name: M6 swallow terminal replacement teardown refusal
mutations.expectRed: persistent invalid_request replacement refusal is terminal before another launch
mutations.cell: a persistent invalid_request replacement refusal is terminal before another launch
